ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RELEASE POLICIES

Pasadena Station is a petroleum pipeline facility distributing product throughout the region.  The RMP-regulated process (stationary source) is limited to the on-site Butane Blending system which allows for the fuel blending of n-Butane into on-site gasoline streams.  The process includes two storage pressure vessels, dual transport offload stations, pump, piping and associated appurtenances. 

Pasadena Station is committed to operating and maintaining processes in a safe, reliable and environmentally sound manner. The Station believes that excellent performance in health, safety, and the environment goes hand in hand with operating reliably, and that outstanding health, safety, and environmental (HES ) performance is of paramount importance.

Pasadena Station is designed, operated and maintained in a manner that protects the environment, as well as the health and safety of its employees, contractors and the community. The Station promotes health, safety, and the environment through programs of awareness, compliance, prevention and protection. These programs include a combination of accidental release prevention and emergency response planning. This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that Pasadena Station has designed and implemented, including:

A. A description of the facility and the use of regulated substance (n-Butane);
B. An overview of the accidental release prevention programs (Program Level 3);
C. A five-year accident history for accidental releases of regulated chemicals;
D. An overview of the emergency response program; and
E. An overview of planned changes to improve safety.

A. STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Butane Blending process has been classified as Program Level 3. No Program 1 or 2 processes are identified. By virtue of the flammable effects associated with Butane, it is necessary to observe certain safety precautions whi

le handling Butane to prevent unnecessary human exposure, to reduce the threat to employee health, and to minimize potential impacts to nearby members of the community.  Safety at the Facility depends upon the manner in which Butane is handled as well as the various safety/control devices incorporated into the design of the process. Furthermore, comprehensive training is provided to employees, which reinforces the safety policies and procedures of the Station.

The Facility has fixed inventories of butane. Butane is received by truck (transports) and stored in two (2) storage pressure vessels.  The butane is pumped to an injection skid for direct injection into various unleaded gasoline streams. Injection quantities are controlled via the injection skid, gasoline analyzer and PLC.  Process safety controls include excess flow valves, low-melting point (<250 degrees Fahrenheit) fusible elements, fail safe valves, vessel high-level shutoffs, emergency shutoff devices on the system and video display terminal, thermal/pressure reliefs, and grounding/interlock devices. Access to the Pasadena Station is restricted to authorized employees, management personnel and authorized contractors/visitors.

B. GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC
PREVENTION MEASURES

Pasadena Station's accidental release prevention programs and emergency planning and response programs help effectively manage the hazards posed to employees, the public, and the environment by on-site hazardous substances . The covered process is regulated by the EPA RMP Rule (40 CFR Part 68) as well as the OSHA Process Safety Management standard (29CFR 1910.119.) The following accident prevention program elements are in place at the Station:

1) Employee Participation,
2) Process Safety Information,
3) Process Hazard Analyses (PHAs,)
4) Standard Operating Procedures,
5) Operator and Maintenance Training,
6) Contractor Management and Evaluations,
7) Pre-startup Safety Review,
8) Mechanical

Integrity with Performance Testing/Preventive Maintenance,
9) Safe Work Permits
10) Management of Change
11) Incident and Process Safety  Event Investigation,
12) Emergency Planning and Response,
13) Internal and Regulatory Compliance Audits, and 
14) Trade Secrets.

These fourteen (14) individual elements of the prevention program work together to prevent and mitigate accidental chemical releases. Pasadena Station and its employees are committed to the standards required by these management programs. In addition to the above elements, there are also specific prevention measures that are employed as part of the Station's operating procedures and engineering/administrative controls to help contain/control, quickly detect and reduce the consequences of a release. These are briefly summarized as follows:

General Risk Reduction and Safety Measures

-Engineering and construction in accordance with recognized industry (ex. NPFA 58) and company standards,
-Equipment properly designed with protection from overpressure (pressure safety relief valves, etc.),
-Updated technical drawings, Piping & Instrument Diagrams and Process Flow Diagrams,
-Operating systems monitored and controlled by trained personnel, 
-Computerized monitoring (local and remote) with control of process operations,
-Redundant safety systems with emergency power,
-Automatic and manual shutdown devices for critical systems,
-Scheduled inspection and testing of instruments, Butane-containing components, and safety devices,
-Controlled/secured facility access,
-Regular safety meetings and safety awareness programs,
-Routinely scheduled safety inspections and audits, and
-Frequent process surveillance by operators.

General Release Mitigation

-Automatic and remotely operated shut-offs to limit release quantity,
-Strategically located valves to isolate leaks,
-Hydrocarbon detectors at key areas to warn of a chemical release and disable the process, and
-Dry-line cooling monitors installed near the butane sto

rage vessels. 

General Emergency Response

-Emergency alert system,
-Periodic emergency training for employees,
-Communication systems with local emergency responders and regulatory agencies,
-Emergency drills with Station personnel, regulatory agencies, and community emergency responders to enhance response skills and coordination among agencies,
-Mutual Aid with Local Fire Departments, and
-Participation with the local LEPC/EMAs.

The Butane Blending process was designed and constructed per National Fire Protection Association's (NFPA's) Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Code (NFPA-58) requirements for LP Gas storage. In addition to the presence of appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of Butane, if a release does occur, emergency response and action plans are in place with response activities being coordinated with the Pasadena Fire Department and Southeast Regional LEPC.

C. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

The Pasadena Station has an excellent record of accident prevention. The Station maintains records for all  accidental chemical releases that occur at its facility.  As this is a newly regulated process, there have been no reportable accidents within the past five (5) years resulting from the release of materials covered under the EPA RMP regulation.

D. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

The Pasadena Station is identified as a Non-Responding Stationary Source and, as such, utilizes outside sources (i.e. municipal and/or refinery fire departments) for offensive-type responses.

In the event of an emergency involving or threat to the Butane Blending process, it is the policy of the Facility to initially contact the Pasadena Fire Department to request their assistance.  The on-site personnel maintain incipient fire and 1st-Responder Operations level training/capabilities.  

A Butane emergency response exercise/drill program is in place that include annual 1st Responder Coordination and Notification Events.

E. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

The Pasadena Stati

on is continually striving to make itself the safest and most reliable workplace possible for its employees, neighbors and the surrounding community.  The Station looks for and actively seeks employee input regarding process safety and improvement in accordance with corporate Employee Participation Program.  All Process Safety Events (as defined in API 754) are electronically recorded, reviewed, and investigated up to utilizing Root Cause methodologies (ex. TapRooT.)
